sanity_expectations: At t=0, C=0 makes the competition term exactly zero, so dN/dt = (per_capita_birth_rate - background_mortality_rate)*N = 60 > 0 and N should initially increase.
Because C obeys dC/dt = crowding_accumulation_rate*N - crowding_relaxation_rate*C with N(0)=100 and C(0)=0, dC/dt at t=0 is 1.5 > 0, so latent crowding should rise from zero after the start.

The trajectory should show an early phase where growth is only weakly suppressed by crowding, followed by stronger suppression once C accumulates; thus two times with similar N can have different dN/dt because C differs.

When C becomes moderate so crowding_saturation_scale*C is order 1, extra increases in C should produce diminishing additional suppression more strongly than a single hyperbola, i.e. dN/dt should flatten versus C at high crowding.

As N increases into the few-hundred range, abundance_crowding_curvature*N is order 1 or larger while abundance_amplification_compression*N also approaches order 1, so the abundance-amplified crowding factor should remain monotone in N but bend over relative to a purely linear 1 + abundance_crowding_curvature*N amplification.
A plausible trajectory is initial increase of N, later deceleration, and approach toward a finite crowded regime rather than unchecked exponential growth over the full window.

rationale: Preserve the validated upstream ODE system contract exactly: although the displayed target expression is structurally an explicit algebraic RHS for dN_dt, the record explicitly supplies a two-state dynamical system with N as target state, C as latent crowding state, one sampled axis t, and freedom_change='none', so N and C remain dynamic variables and all listed coefficients remain fixed parameters. The chosen parameter set keeps low-density net growth positive (per_capita_birth_rate - background_mortality_rate = 0.6), ensuring initial increase from N(0)=100 while C(0)=0 produces an early near-exponential rise. Delayed crowding is made observable by using a moderate accumulation rate (0.015) and slower relaxation (0.3), so C lags N and later becomes appreciable over the same trajectory. The C-saturation argument crowding_saturation_scale*C is designed to move from near 0 early to order 1 during the trajectory, exposing the stronger-than-hyperbolic high-C compression through high_crowding_compression = 0.5 without placing the whole run deep in saturation. The abundance-amplification curvature abundance_crowding_curvature = 0.01 makes abundance_crowding_curvature*N already order 1 around N~100 and larger during growth, while abundance_amplification_compression = 0.005 keeps abundance_amplification_compression*N small-to-moderate at low abundance but order 1 as N rises into a few hundred, so the new high-abundance bending of the amplification factor is active but not collapsed to its recovery limit. This should expose the intended sequence of mechanisms along one trajectory: early low-crowding growth close to the simpler ancestors, followed by delayed crowding suppression, then visible high-N compression of abundance-amplified competition and stronger flattening of additional suppression at high C. No observation noise is added; outputs are exact numerical solutions of the inherited system.
